1) Restore SLAs: For customer-scoped restores (data for a single customer), what is Redwood's standard SLA for a full restore from archival/backups? Please specify differences between Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (VPC / on-prem).

2) Backup scope & retention: What exact artifacts are included in backups/archives (application logs, audit trails, raw prompts, model KV cache, user-generated files)? What are retention windows for each artifact class and where are those archives stored (region/cold storage)?

Hi Elena — thanks, good set of questions. High-level answers inline (short) and I'm looping in Marissa (Compliance) and will have Rishi (Security) validate the technical specifics; attaching our current retention matrix and backup runbook for context.

1) Restore SLAs: For Dedicated and Private deployments we operate on a customer-initiated restore SLA target of 72 hours for a full customer-scoped restore (subject to scope/size). Hosted API restores are handled on a best-effort basis and may require additional coordination; we document expected time windows in the runbook.

2) Backup scope & retention: Backups include: audit logs, system logs, configuration metadata, and customer data payloads. Model runtime artifacts (KV cache) are not persisted beyond session unless explicitly stored by customer. Retention windows are covered in the attached matrix — please see the "artifact retention" tab. Archives are encrypted at rest and stored in the EU region for NovaMed by default.

3) Prompt handling: By default, short-lived prompts used in generation are treated as ephemeral — persisted in hot logs for up to 30 days (for debugging/quality) and then moved/trimmed in archival snapshots; customers can opt-in to longer retention. We support prompt-level erasure requests; typical operational completion is 14 business days for Hosted, and 7 business days for Dedicated/Private where we control the storage.

4) Restore evidence: Attaching a stripped sample runbook and retention matrix. We'll follow up with a redacted restore report and a recent test-run summary.

Sharing attachments: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx; backup-restore-runbook.pdf

Cheers,

Jordan / Marissa — quick technical confirm to use in the customer reply. Current operational detail we can share (redacted where required):

- Backup cadence: incremental snapshots every 24 hours, weekly full snapshot. Differential deltas are retained for 90 days in warm storage; full weekly snapshots are retained 400 days in cold storage (EU region for NovaMed).
- Artifact list: application logs (90 days hot / 400 days cold), audit trails (365 days), customer-submitted files and persisted user objects (retained per contract / default 400 days), raw prompts (hot logs up to 30 days; not included in long-term archival by default).
- Restore process: customer-scoped restores are executed from cold snapshots and validated with checksum/audit; estimated operational SLA 72 hours for Dedicated/Private for datasets < 10TB; exceptions for extremely large or fragmented datasets. Hosted API subject to queuing & service dependencies — provide best-effort ETA.
- Evidence: We can include a redacted restore run report (date, snapshot id, duration, verification steps) and our restore-runbook PDF. For NovaMed's auditors we should also include SOC 2 test report excerpts; Marissa will advise what to attach.

I'll prepare a redacted sample restore report (sccs-evidence.zip) and handoff to Marissa for attestation statements.

Hi Elena — following up with consolidated responses and the artifacts you requested. Answers below are suitable for inclusion in your DPA annex; where you need formal attestation we can provide the redacted artifacts noted.

A. Restore SLA (customer-scoped)
- Dedicated & Private (VPC/on-prem): standard operational target = 72 hours for datasets under 10TB. Larger restores are scoped and scheduled; we provide timeline estimates within 48 hours of request.
- Hosted API: restores of customer data are supported but timing is subject to shared infrastructure constraints; we will provide an ETA after request intake.

B. Backup scope & retention (summary)
- Application logs: 90 days hot, archived to cold storage for 400 days.
- Audit trails: retained 365 days (per SOC 2 baseline).
- Customer persisted files & objects: default 400 days unless contractually specified.
- Model runtime KV cache: not persisted beyond session unless explicitly stored by customer.

C. Prompt retention & erasure
- Default: transient prompts are kept in hot logs for up to 30 days for debugging/quality monitoring. They are not persisted to long-term archival unless the customer elects explicit retention.
- Erasure requests: we support prompt-level erasure. Operational completion: Hosted — up to 14 business days; Dedicated/Private — up to 7 business days.

D. Evidence provided
- retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (attached) — artifact classes and windows
- backup-restore-runbook.pdf (attached) — procedural steps for restore and verification
- sccs-evidence.zip (attached) — redacted sample restore report + SOC 2 excerpts (for auditor review)

Related links: https://redwood.example.com/kb/retention-restore (public KB), JIRA-INF-724 (internal ticket that tracked a recent multi-tenant restore test).
